title: Experts disagree on shared/references/evidence-levels.md
context:
Chief architect: The two notes are complementary, not opposed: the architect fixes the structure (one new shared reference) and the security auditor fixes a rule that lives inside it (the install signal tests the dot-paqad directory existence only and never reads it). Both hold; the existence-only install-signal rule is written into evidence-levels.md. No owner decision is needed.

Target: shared/references/evidence-levels.md
- security-auditor: The install signal must test for the EXISTENCE of a .paqad/ directory only and never read its contents, honouring the never-read list; reading .paqad/ would expose runtime state and secrets.
- application-architect: The three levels, their detection, the source line, the nudge and the code-only finder belong in ONE new shared reference (RL-04a1, PLG-9), consumed by six skills, not restated in each skill; it must stay provider-neutral (PLG-4), capability-worded (PLG-7), under 100 lines and free of em/en dashes.
